Fix empty guest heap and missing CD callback; boot reaches opening movie

DotR calls SetupHeap(0x1FE0000, 0x20000), above the runtime's 0x1F00000
heap limit, so the heap was empty, every malloc returned 0, init failed and
main returned to ra=0 (the pc=0x0 ticks). Patch 0003 moves the runtime's
RPC/TLS/boot-mode pools and callback stacks below the ELF (0x80000-0xFFFFF)
and lets an explicit heap reach 32 MB.

The game's SDFS layer then waited forever for its sceCdCallback handler,
which the runtime ignored. Patch 0004 stores the callback and queues it
after each sceCdRead.

both and replaces up to 100 queries per finished game with one.

[vk] Take the provoking vertex and logic operation the 3D engine sets

Two pieces of 3D engine state reached no pipeline. PROVOKING_VERTEX (0x5A1) at 1 makes a
primitive's last vertex feed its flat inputs, GL's and NVN's default, where Vulkan takes
the first: with VK_EXT_provoking_vertex's provokingVertexLast the pipeline now asks for the
last one. LOGIC_OP (0x671, with the operation at 0x672 numbered as GL's 0x1500 CLEAR to
0x150F SET, VkLogicOp's order) now replaces blending on integer and normalized targets
with logicOp. A device without either says so once in the log.

A list of the 3D reg

[vk] Read raw surface loads from any 4-byte color format

SULD.D.32 takes texel coordinates and returns a texel's 32 bits whatever the header's
components are (its shaders pass the pixel position unscaled). tex_from_tic gave a raw
load an R32_UINT view only of an RGBA8 header. One game's post-processing reads its
A2B10G10R10 targets and R32_UINT masks this way, and each of those draws was skipped:
the bind returned no descriptor set. Any uncompressed, unconverted color format of 4-byte
texels now has the view, a target of another format through rt_crop's bit copy.

Let defense wards fire as soon as their charge-up ends

fired up to 100 ticks after a biter came into range, and those whose
target died mid-charge took another 75 ticks. The ward inherited the
laser turret's slow barrel rotation (it had to face the target before
charging) and its long stand-down, and woke only once enemies were
already in range. The shard faces its target instantly now, wakes at 12
tiles and stands down in 12 ticks: the first volley comes 55 ticks
sooner and follow-ups 17 ticks sooner.

fix(scheduler): recover work that changed nothing without asking a person

When a scheduler stopped, every Run it was executing became
outcome_unknown and every reply it was sending stayed interrupted. Only
a person could resolve them, so one crash stopped a long game until
someone noticed, and the member whose reply was cut off was never asked
again.

A Run that never started a tool call or submitted harness work changed
nothing outside itself. Such a Run now fails with side_effects
not_started: its reply is queued again, and its task fails so the
requester can retry it. Runs that used a tool

fix(work): let a live job bind its own claimed run

The scheduler's reconcile treated a work item that was still queued but
already had a claimed Run as a crash leftover and recorded it as running.
When the job that made the claim was alive and about to bind it, the two
writes raced on the item's revision: whichever lost failed with "stale
work revision". A losing job failed its Run ("cannot bind work Run"); a
losing scheduler exited, which stopped every reply in a long game.

Reconcile now leaves a running claim alone while its job is live and only
records claims whose job is gone.

(about 110 in the first 400 s of the Michigan State film), and every
decoder silently drops them. The worker numbered frames by counting
reads, so its frame numbers fell further behind the picture as the game
went on: 98 frames off at 5 1/2 minutes, 410 frames (6.8 s) at 25
minutes. Detection, play videos, overlays, calibration, re-ID crops and
team colours all drifted with it, which is why boxes slid off players in
later plays.

fix: re-key cached matches when a new API key changes PUUIDs

Riot encrypts PUUIDs per API key. After switching keys, a lookup gets a
new PUUID, but the player's matches were cached under the old one, so
has_match() skipped them and the profile came back with 0 games.

store_matches() now takes the player's PUUID. When a cached match has
no participant with it, the match is fetched again and its participant
rows are re-keyed to the new PUUIDs (matched by champion, which is
unique per game) instead of being inserted a second time.

fix(d3d): reclaim heap pages of FM6 placement textures overwritten by newer ones

FM6 streams new textures into game memory still owned by older texture
objects it never releases; each kept its own D3D12 copy, so placed heap
memory grew without bound. When a new placement texture covers the game
memory of an older live one, the older one becomes an orphan: its heap
pages return to the allocator after a hold (PlacementReclaimHoldMs, 2 s)
and new textures alias them, as on the console. Refreshes of orphans are
skipped and counted. debug.ini PlacementReclaim turns it off.

bsd: Linux errno numbers and O_NONBLOCK 0x800 (SM35 now joins the 35-player match relay)

The Switch's socket library uses Linux errno numbers (EAGAIN 11, EINPROGRESS 115,
EISCONN 106...), not FreeBSD's. SMB35's socket wrapper checks for 115 after a
non-blocking connect; with 36 it never saw the relay connection as pending and
connected again every frame until it gave up, so a match ended at "Here we go...".
Fcntl's O_NONBLOCK is Linux's 0x800 too (the game asked for non-blocking and got a
blocking socket). GetPeerName answers ENOTCONN while a connect is still in progress.

RECOMP_BSD_TRACE=1

Oblivion went black on its first boot on the LLVM recompiler: a thread
called abort(). The game starts its task manager's thread from inside the
manager's constructor and finishes the object afterwards. On a PS3 the new
thread takes microseconds to start; here the main thread's turn ended just
after the start and the new thread ran first, on a half-built object. The
"Cannot allocate" memory messages appear on every boot and were not the
cause.

D88: an inline draw followed by the game's own packets is still drawn

the draw's end or past it within the same segment (less than 64 KB further): the game committed the draw and then
wrote packets of its own before the next device call. Those packets are not read. A write pointer short of the end,
or in another segment, still drops the draw.

The repetition rule: Stockfish's, a draw inside the search or on the third time

Search.IsRepetition called any position seen once before since the last
capture or pawn move a draw, the game before the search included, so a
move back to a position from a few moves ago scored 0.00 at once (TURNS.md,
"The false draw": 13 lost games turned on one). Now a repeat is a draw only
if the earlier occurrence is inside the search, after the root, or if the
position is there for the third time. The root itself counts as the game's:
coming back to it once is not a draw.

Don't crash when a locked chunk is polluted before its first check (#1613)

Terraforming draws each locked chunk's pollution progress the first
time it checks the chunk below the threshold. A chunk that already had
enough pollution at its first check had no progress text yet, and
destroying it errored and stopped the game. That can happen when a
chunk is generated next to heavily polluted land: the checks go round
every locked chunk one per tick, so pollution can spread in first.

  AES-256

Keep browser saves going when a save reply is lost

On a slow or dropped connection the server could store a save while the
reply never reached the tab (nginx logged 499/408 around these). The tab
then resent with the old revision, got 409 and stopped the game with
"Your save changed in another tab". After a 409 the tab now reads the
cloud save: if it holds a snapshot this tab sent without confirmation,
it adopts that revision and keeps syncing; anything else is still a real
conflict. Save requests also wait 45 s (the server's timeout) instead of
aborting at 15 s.

Tilt: Steady the tilt input with the gyroscope where there is one

sensor noise and jumps when the device is shaken. Now, when gyro data is
coming in, a complementary filter integrates the gyro rates and only pulls
the result toward the accelerometer with a 0.5 s time constant, trusting
the accelerometer less the further it reads from 1g. The fused vector goes
through the same ProcessTilt path, so calibration and sensitivity work as
before. Without a gyro, nothing changes.

Fix Jolt's double get-up after a ragdoll

A knockdown gives the ped the game's own TASK_COMPLEX_FALL_AND_GET_UP in
an event-response slot. Jolt ragdolls the body and then adds its own
TASK_SIMPLE_GET_UP as the physical response, which has priority; when
it ends, the game's fall task resumes and the ped gets up a second time
(e.g. after falling off a bike).

Hook Jolt's call to CPedIntelligence::AddTaskPhysResponse and, when it
adds a get-up, abort and remove the waiting fall-and-get-up task. Only
the traced Jolt build (September 22) is patched.

type the C gives it in between. FontPrintCenter, FontPrintCenterSmall
and FontPrintCenterLarge (and FontPrintLarge/Small, the right-aligned

it on to FontPrint's u64, which keeps all 64 bits in its first palette
slot and its GIF colour words. The port carried 32 bits and passed
them on zero-extended: FontPrint's a2 was 0x000000008040F040 where
retail's is 0xFFFFFFFF8040F040.

D3D9: bindings held per frame instead of a reference count per bind

Textures, vertex and index buffers, declarations and shaders bound by the
device take a private reference when first bound; binding them again
only notes the frame (no atomic). A Present gives back the references of
objects neither bound now nor used in the frame before; Reset and the
application's release of the device give back all. Each atomic made the
game thread wait for its pending stores (the worker's command chunks),
and draws bind several objects each.

Reset the winner when a finished game is undone in manual mode.

After the last board died, manageGame() set gameActive to false and
m_winner to the winner before waiting for the arrow keys. Undoing a move
then revived the board but left both in place, so the next forward step
ended the game in an unfinished position and the log recorded the old
winner. The main thread also never removed the winner text once shown.

Clear m_winner and set gameActive again on undo, and delete the winner
text in update() when m_winner goes back to 0.

Star Realms: tournament stops early with SPRT (#144)

tournament --sprt runs Wald's sequential probability ratio test on bot A's
wins and losses after each game (--h0, --h1, --alpha, --beta; --games is the
limit) and stops once it decides. It reports the decision, games played,
A's win rate with its Wilson interval, and the LLR and its bounds. With
--jobs N games are played ahead in N processes but decided in seed order,
so the result is one process's.

From the original project (ZeldaWWHDRecomp 850b5435): the board hands its pooled hit and miss models
out by scanning the cells in column order, so a shot into an earlier cell gives later markers other

start, the save runs on the calling thread as before.

Co-Authored-By: Claude O

Pace SPU2 AutoDMA at the playback rate so New Game's BGM change completes

KCEJEAST streams BGM through libspu2 AutoDMA (ADMAS set, 128 KB halves
re-armed from the DMA4 IRQ). The IOP emulator completed every SPU2 DMA at
bus speed, so the driver reported buffers consumed in microseconds and the
EE transfer queue overflowed; New Game then waited forever for the BGM
change behind the black fade. Patch 0012 completes AutoDMA transfers after
bytes * 192 IOP cycles (48 kHz 16-bit stereo).

The game now leaves the fade wait and hangs on overlay code at 0x1E00080
(#19).

Fixes #12

Steadier 3D with precise vertices

Precise vertices only knew a corner's float position when the GTE had
stored it into the packet itself (swc2). The game copies about 42 % of
its projected positions through the CPU, so only 57 % of the corners got
their precise position and the rest still wobbled. Now the GTE keeps the
float position and depth of what it projected lately by value too, and a
corner whose address is unknown is looked up by its value: 93 % of the
corners are precise. A value two different vertices rounded to in the
same frame is not used, so no corner gets another one's depth.

Let a dropped player rejoin their match slot

A client that disconnects mid-match can join again and get its slot back
with its cards and score. The host matches it by a per-process rejoin key,
or by name if the game was restarted. The rejoiner sits out a battle
already under way and plays from the next one, or picks right away during
a card pick. If a drop leaves fewer than two players, the host holds the
match for 45 seconds before ending it.

Adds --dropat=N (autojoin) and --nobots (autohost) to test it end to end.

lyrac run --live: a change swapped into the running program, its state kept

--watch restarts the program on every save. --live builds the change as the
next generation, checks it against generation 0, and loads it into the
running program at its next loop turn in main, so a game keeps its window
and its world. Where a change cannot be swapped safely (main changed, a
type's shape or layout changed, a top-level let is new or retyped, the
links changed, no answer within 2s) it restarts as --watch does and says
why. macOS only; elsewhere it is --watch.

a game's own store to the register moved the counter, and 30 Hz games

in 60 Hz render mode and its bit 1 otherwise, and only bits 0-1 come
from the game (MAME videoctl_r). vcop, desert, daytona and vf2 frames
are unchanged, apart from the phase of vcop's reticle colour cycle.

Stop retrying a failed adaptive sync switch every frame, either way

When turning adaptive sync off failed after a game left, set_vrr
reported it still on and vrr_failed only covered enabling, so the
switch was retried, with a warning, on every frame. A failed enable,
on the other hand, was never tried again for the rest of the session.

policy has wanted the other state (the next game, or the game leaving).
The decision is a small function with unit tests; the switch itself
needs DRM hardware (docs/hardware-test.md, VRR).

upload into 1/16 each: with zero offsets the blur is a copy.

Add a solver for known deals: nested Monte Carlo search

With the tile order fixed the game is a deterministic puzzle. Nested
Monte Carlo Search (Cazenave 2009): level 0 plays the rest of the game
with a fast policy on the real remaining order; level n tries each
candidate move, judges it by a level n-1 search, and follows the best
complete sequence found so far, so the result never gets worse. The top
level spreads candidates over threads; seeds derive from step and
candidate, so results don't depend on the thread count. verify replays a
solution and checks every move is legal.

Renderer v2: the upload worker sleeps instead of spinning a core

libc++ on Windows truncates a timed wait's time left to whole milliseconds
for SleepConditionVariableSRW, so the worker's 1 ms predicate wait
returned at once and looped for the whole millisecond: 95% of a core.
One 2 ms wait sleeps ~1 ms; queued jobs still wake it (8 or more) or run
in the submission that waits for them. Measured in First Light: the
worker at 13% of a core, the game at 317% instead of 428%, GPU load 80%
instead of 71% at the same frame rate or a little higher.

[runtime] Ignore a SIGSEGV or SIGBUS that no access raised

A game crashed right after a debugger detached. The report's fault address
was 0x3e80021d87e, which is no address: it is the sender's uid (1000) and pid
read as si_addr, so the signal had been sent, not raised by an access. When
gdbserver detaches holding a fault it stopped a thread for (one of the
runtime's own guest-memory traps, which GDB is told to pass), the kernel
delivers it again as SI_USER from the parent, without the fault's address. The
crash handler found no frozen range at that "address" and reported a crash.

Exact chip bus timing for the 68000

The CPU's accesses now come through cpuBus: before each chip access the
rest of the machine runs up to it, and it waits for an even colour clock
the bitplanes and the Copper leave free. Accesses happen at their own
time within an instruction, and a Copper waking mid-instruction takes
the CPU's slots. Default on (--exact-bus=false for the old forecast);
68020 and up keep the forecast.

The full suite passes both ways; the game sweep reaches the same screens,
some later (the 68000's even-slot alignment makes CPU-bound code ~10%
slower, as on the A500).

Build nine of our own games with stages against the computer or the clock

Chess, drafts, Bao and Connect Four are played against a computer that gets
stronger each stage. 8-ball pool is played against a computer whose aim gets
better each stage. Snake, Block Stacker and 2048 get faster or set higher
targets each stage, and Sudoku gets harder each stage.

Every game's rules live in one module that both the browser and the server

SABounce 0.3.7: fix opaque white headlight beams

Looking at a car from the front while it was stretched by the bounce could
turn its headlight beams into solid white quads. The game computes the beam
alpha as (1 - |dot(toCamera, forward)|) * 32 and stores it in a byte; the
stretched forward axis (longer than 1) made that value negative, and the byte
wrapped to nearly 255. The beam now gets a unit-length forward axis, and the
headlight's forward offset that it no longer scales is added to its position.

emitted straight-line: nine in ten of the game's pixel shaders and every

An own buffer is checked against the written-page tracking each time
the caches start a new epoch, and that query takes the range's host
address. buf_get found it with gmem_ptr every time, translating the GPU
range through the page table, and the translation was 1.6% of one
game's GPU thread. The address only changes when the GPU mappings or
the guest memory under them do, and vkr_mapping_end sees every such
change. So an entry keeps its guest offset with the generation of the
mappings (vk_buf_mapping_changed bumps it)

reads a Surf scattered in memory, and the walks were 2.6% of the GPU
thread's samples.

the one there before it makes or takes another. So the live ones now sit
in an open-addressed table keyed by address, kept as targets are made,

The game's disc reads run on a worker thread

ADXF_ReadNw starts the read on a worker and returns; ADXF_GetStat (and
a stop, a close, the next read) waits for it, so a poll sees the read
finished on the frame it would if it were done at once. The game asks on
one frame and polls on the next, so the read has the rest of the frame
and the frame's rendering. A rollback snapshot waits for every read
first (sf_files_sync), so no read lands in memory while it is copied.

and estimates tau, the between-hitter SD of the true Coors effect, by
method of moments with a 2,000-draw bootstrap over hitters. The noise term
uses each hitter's own per-PA variance, a game design effect, and the
variance of the error in his estimated batter level (amendment A-4).

T053: fix audio crackle (patches 0060-0062, audio_pacing override)

The music crackled because 66% of the mixed blocks were silent: MultiStream's update thread
runs one mixer round per block, but its 5 ms nap plus the (slow) SPU mixer made a round 8-15 ms,
so the game wrote every 2nd-3rd ring slot. Faster audio SPU paths (native float, lean LS, x86
rotqby family) and the nap scaled to 0 give 0% silent blocks and 0-1 block-edge clicks over
42-65 s windows (was 860). tools/audio_wav_report.py judges an AUDIO_WAV capture.

well after the launcher started the game. By then another window, often
the launcher's own, may be in front, and a game that opens behind it is
easy to miss. The launcher already lets the game process take the
foreground (AllowSetForegroundWindow in launcher_platform_win32.cpp), so
the game asks for it when it shows the window. Windows only; the other
platforms are unchanged.

no payload). RuneLite only fires its GameTick event, replays deferred
events such as VarbitChanged and advances its tick count when that packet
arrives, so without it a client on our server never sees a game tick:
the Tick Recorder's first two recordings had every line on tick 1.

Queue ServerTickEnd as the last packet of each real tick, after player and
NPC info and before the flush. A paused cycle still sends player info to
keep the client connected but is not a tick, so

sdl: Set the EEPROM mask for EEPROM games

eepromMask starts out zero and only eepromSetSize() gives it a value.
Until then every ROM read passes the EEPROM address test in
gbaInline.h and is answered by the EEPROM state machine instead of the
cartridge, so a game with an EEPROM save reads zeros from its ROM and
never gets past its first frame: Super Mario Advance boots to a white
screen. The wx port, the libretro core and frame_dump all call
eepromSetSize() after choosing the save type; the SDL port never did,
on any platform, since ec46bf83 introduced the mask.

the bot now plays whichever guarantees the longest game, at random when several
tie. Length is measured with the bot stretching and the visitor cutting short,
neither giving up a win it holds. Replaces the fewest-winning-replies trap.

finishing reply, so the kill is the only winning hit. Tested against an
independent search over every position for m up to 9.

feat(jev): Jev decides chat status, model hints, ⌘K and lane emoji, with a free → bonus fallback (#1858)

* feat(jev): shared Jev decision helper (ai.jevDecide / ai.jevStatus)

One machine-local helper every ADE feature uses to ask OpenCode Zen's free
jev-1.13-free decision model a typed noul/choice/score question. Gated on an
unexpired OpenCode Zen sign-in read from opencode.db, off via
ai.chat.smartDecisionsEnabled. Breaker, call cap, LRU cache, jev.summary and
jev.breaker_opened logs. Every failure answers null so callers keep their
current logic. Renderer: window.ade.ai.jevDecide(request,
